displayName: loop-sessions: lifecycle-only session spawns over the rule

conditions.displayName: fleet empty-start rate above 0.6 for an hour
machines over the per-device empty-start rule in an hour

documentation.content:
Either more than 60% of the fleet's sessions in the last day ended before a first prompt, or at least one machine is over the per-device rule (twenty or more lifecycle-only spawns in a day, at least half of its sessions). These are `claude` processes started non-interactively and closed before anything is sent: a GUI host spawning one per open project, or a script running `claude -p`, `-c` or `--resume` with stdin closed. The server tags them `empty` and hides them; nothing is broken server-side, and the people generating them usually do not know.

The `fleet empty_start` line names the person, the cwd set and the launcher-probe recipe (a one-line SessionStart hook that appends the parent process, bundle id, terminal and entrypoint to `~/.loop/sessions/logs/launcher.log`): `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="fleet empty_start"' --freshness=1h --format='value(jsonPayload.email,jsonPayload.empties,jsonPayload.total,jsonPayload.cwds,jsonPayload.recipe)'`. Send the person the recipe; a day of that log names the launcher. Mute the row on /admin/fleet once the message is sent, with the date in the note, so the same name does not page daily.

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-empty-sessions
